html:
The K'áálǫ Got'ine are a Dene group of the Sahtu region in the Northwest Territories of Canada. The map places them between the Mackenzie River and the northwest arm of Great Bear Lake. Got'ine means "people of".

Like other Sahtu Dene they hunted caribou and moose, trapped and fished the lakes. Fur posts of the Hudson's Bay Company at Fort Good Hope and on the Mackenzie drew them into trade. Today they are covered by the land claim of the Sahtu Dene and Métis. Little is published about this group separately.
